name: Formula G
oneLine: Every game runs the same six-stage sequence: Con + Gimmick = Response -> Switch -> Crossup -> Payoff.
whatYouDid: You traced Mei's two weeks of quiet overtime through Formula G and pinpointed the exact line - "No one appreciates what I do around here!" - as the Switch, not the Payoff or the Crossup.
confusion: People look for the game in the blow-up at the end and miss that the Switch, not the final feeling, is the diagnostic moment - everything before it can look like an ordinary helpful pattern.

fromBook.quote: Con + Gimmick = Response -> Switch -> Crossup -> Payoff

expand.definition: Con is the ulterior hook (often non-verbal); Gimmick is the other player's weak spot that buys into it; Response is the repeated transaction run that follows; the Switch is the sudden role-flip; the Crossup is the shared moment of confusion right after; the Payoff is the racket feeling both players collect.
expand.otherFraming: Berne's earlier, Games People Play-era definition skipped the Switch entirely and just meant any ulterior-transaction sequence ending in a payoff - TA Today calls that version "racketeering" instead, and reserves "game" for sequences that include the Switch.
expand.tryThisToday: Pick one recent mildly bad interaction and write its six Formula G stages in one line each - if you can't find a Switch, it was probably racketeering, not a game.
